{{Short description|Geometry Theorem}}
[[File:Haruki theorem.svg|thumb|upright=1.5|Illustration of Haruki's Theorem:<br/><math>\frac{s_1}{s_2} \cdot \frac{s_3}{s_4} \cdot \frac{s_5}{s_6} = 1</math>]]
'''Haruki's Theorem''' says that given three intersecting circles that only intersect each other at two points that the lines connecting the inner intersecting points to the outer satisfy:
<math display="block"> s_1 \cdot s_3 \cdot s_5 = s_2 \cdot s_4 \cdot s_6</math>
where <math> s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4,  s_5, s_6 </math> are the measure of [[Line segment|segments]] connecting the inner and outer intersection points.<ref>{{cite journal |title=On a metrical theorem in geometry of circles |first=Hiroshi |last=Haruki |year=1972 |journal=Colloquium Mathematicum |volume=25 |pages=99-102 |doi=10.4064/cm-25-1-99-102 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Wisstein|first1=Eric|title=Haruki's Theorem|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/HarukisTheorem.html|website=Wolfram MathWorld|publisher=Wolfram MathWorld|accessdate=19 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=[[Alexander Bogomolny|Bogomolny, Alexander]]|title=Cut the Knot|url=http://www.cut-the-knot.org/proofs/HarukiTheorem.shtml|accessdate=19 August 2015}}</ref><ref>[[Ross Honsberger]]: ''Episodes in Nineteenth and Twentieth Century Euclidean Geometry''. MAA, 1995, p. 144-146</ref>

The theorem is named after the Japanese mathematician [[Hiroshi Haruki]].
